summary: This section explains who takes charge when the top office of the Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal becomes vacant or the head is away. If the President or Chairperson leaves due to death, resignation, or any other reason, the senior-most Member steps in until a new one is appointed. Similarly, if they are unable to work due to illness or absence, the senior-most Member handles their duties until they return.
points: The senior-most Member acts as the President or Chairperson if that office becomes vacant due to death, resignation, or other reasons.
The acting President or Chairperson serves until a new one is formally appointed and takes office.
If the President or Chairperson cannot work because of illness, absence, or any other cause, the senior-most Member takes over their functions.
The senior-most Member only discharges these duties until the regular President or Chairperson returns to work.
example: At the National Company Law Tribunal, the Chairperson Mr. Sharma falls seriously ill and has to take a long leave of absence to recover. Because Mr. Sharma is unable to discharge his functions owing to illness, the rules state that someone must step in. Therefore, Ms. Rao, who is the senior-most Member of the Tribunal, takes over the duties of the Chairperson. Ms. Rao continues to handle all the necessary functions until Mr. Sharma fully recovers and resumes his duties at the office.

terms.meaning: A specialized legal body established to deal with specific types of disputes or cases.
A situation where a job or official position is empty because no one is holding it.
To carry out the duties and responsibilities of a job.

watch: Do not confuse a temporary absence or illness where the head will return with a permanent vacancy caused by resignation or death.
